title: Finite thick approximation of the connecting component across one triangle
statement: Let C be triangulated with coproducts [def-weil-triangulated-category], E:I→C a compact family [def-pc-compact-object], and T=(Z→Y→W→Z[1]) distinguished with Z a coproduct of shifts of the E_i. Suppose every map from every compact object to Y factors through an object in a finite thick envelope [def-pc-thick-closure] of the family. For any compact K and f:K→W there is K→Q→W with Q in such a finite thick envelope whose composite agrees with f after W→Z[1]. Equality before the connecting map is not asserted.

source.place: Tag 09SP, induction step through the cone construction, before lifting the difference; compactness closure is Lemma 13.37.2

proof.text: Use [lem-sc-compact-objects-thick] to install the triangulated and retract-closed property R of compact objects. The finite unshifted generator sum is compact by finite-product closure and the finite product/coproduct isomorphism. Thus its thick envelope lies in R by triangEnvelope_le_iff.

Shift the given isomorphism Z≅the coproduct of E_i[m], use the shift/coproduct comparison and shiftFunctorAdd, and apply [lem-sc-compact-coproduct-finite-thick-support] to f followed by the connecting morphism. Obtain K→Q₀→Z[1] in a finite thick envelope. Set F=Q₀[-1] and identify F[1] with Q₀. Fullness of the shift functor produces F→Z whose shift is the second factor. The first factor becomes g:K→F[1]. The resulting g followed by the shifted map is f followed by the connecting morphism. F stays in the finite thick envelope by shift closure and is compact.

Complete g to F→K'→K→F[1] by distinguished_cocone_triangle₂ [def-weil-triangulated-category]. By compactness closure [lem-sc-compact-objects-thick], K' is compact. The connecting square extends to a triangle morphism via complete_distinguished_triangle_morphism₂, giving K'→Y. Apply the assumed factorization property of Y to obtain K'→Q'→Y. Complete F→K'→Q' to a distinguished triangle F→Q'→Q→F[1]. Apply complete_distinguished_triangle_morphism twice to get K→Q→W. Their third commutative squares prove agreement with f after the connecting morphism. The union of the finite supports contains F and Q' in its thick envelope, since the smaller generator sums retract from the union sum. Closure under cones puts Q there.

proof_origin.place: Tag 09SP, cone construction before exactness correction, now proved in Lean using compactness closure (Tag 09QH)

lean.statement:
theorem compact_triangle_connecting_approximation
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [HasZeroObject C] [HasShift C ℤ]
    [Preadditive C] [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor C n).Additive]
    [Pretriangulated C] [IsTriangulated C] [HasCoproducts.{w} C]
    {I : Type w} (E : I → C) (hcompact : ∀ i : I, IsCompactObject (E i))
    (T : Triangle C) (hT : T ∈ distTriang C)
    (hZ : ∃ (J : Type w) (i : J → I) (m : J → ℤ),
      Nonempty (T.obj₁ ≅ ∐ fun j : J ↦ (E (i j))⟦m j⟧))
    (hY : ∀ (K : C), IsCompactObject K → ∀ (f : K ⟶ T.obj₂),
      ∃ (S : Finset I) (Q : C) (a : K ⟶ Q) (b : Q ⟶ T.obj₂),
        (ObjectProperty.singleton (∐ fun i : {i : I // i ∈ S} ↦ E i.val)).triangEnvelope Q ∧
          a ≫ b = f)
    (K : C) (hK : IsCompactObject K) (f : K ⟶ T.obj₃) :
    ∃ (S : Finset I) (Q : C) (a : K ⟶ Q) (b : Q ⟶ T.obj₃),
      (ObjectProperty.singleton (∐ fun i : {i : I // i ∈ S} ↦ E i.val)).triangEnvelope Q ∧
        (a ≫ b) ≫ T.mor₃ = f ≫ T.mor₃
